content.text: {"prompt": "A square, purely nonrepresentational abstract painting in oil and cold wax that fills the entire canvas edge to edge, with no frame, border, wall, room, or gallery setting. The composition is about steady attention held under pressure. Most of the left and lower field is a broad, calm expanse of deep ultramarine and slate grey, scraped with a wide knife into long horizontal drags so the surface looks patient and slightly translucent, with thin glazes of pale blue-green showing underneath. A large area of bare, warm off-white ground is left open near the upper left as quiet breathing space. Cutting diagonally through the right half is a dense, agitated band of cadmium red, burnt orange, and hot magenta, built from short, fast, stabbing strokes laid over one another until the paint is thick and ridged. At its edge the heat breaks apart into scattered flecks and dry-brush streaks that drift into the cool field and dull to rust and ash violet where they meet it. Small, deliberate patches of bright lemon yellow and a single narrow vein of luminous mint appear in the middle of the turbulence, like points of clarity that stay unresolved. Heavy impasto and thin washes sit against each other. Some passages have drips and scumbled, sanded-back layers, and others are sharp, clean-edged planes of flat colour. The rhythm is a slow, steady pulse in the cool areas against fast, jagged syncopation in the hot areas. The spatial tension comes from the unequal weight of the two zones, with the calm mass leaning against the burning edge and neither side winning. There are no objects, figures, faces, symbols, letters, numbers, text, or horizon lines. The look is raw, tactile, and gestural, with visible bristle marks, palette-knife ridges, and a matte-to-satin sheen, lit evenly like a flat scan of the canvas surface."}
